finding: cap_requested_schema now DECODES a string-encoded requestedSchema from an EXTERNAL MCP server. If the decode ran after the x-ziee-askuser strip, a server could forge the trusted rich-UX marker by simply JSON-encoding its schema. Verified the order is size-cap -> decode -> strip, so the strip is last and sees the decoded object.
DoS: an oversized encoded schema must not be parsed. Verified the size measurement runs on the RAW value before any from_str, so a multi-megabyte string is dropped without allocating its parse.

The refusal text interpolates serde_json::Error's Display. Confirmed that carries only a position ('expected ident at line 1 column 2'), never the payload's content, so a hostile argument cannot smuggle attacker text into a model-visible message via the error path. Pinned by a new test.
Unbounded unwrapping would be a DoS on model/server-controlled input. Verified MAX_STRING_UNWRAPS bounds a for-loop (not a while-let); a 10-deep nesting terminates at the bound.

coerce_args_in_place used slot.take(), which leaves the slot as Null on the error path. All four callers pass a clone AND propagate with ?, so it cannot bite today - but a future caller that logged-and-continued would silently operate on a payload whose argument had been ERASED. Changed to clone-then-assign (the clone only occurs on the already-wrong path).

Empty and whitespace-only strings, and surrounding whitespace on a valid payload, were unverified. Probed: '' / '   ' / newline+tab are refused; '  {"a":1}  ' decodes (models emit padded JSON). Added as a test rather than left to reasoning.

prepare_ask_user_schema rejects a supplied object schema with no `properties`, which also rejects a root-level oneOf/anyOf schema. Accepted narrowing: SEP-1330 elicitation is a flat object of properties and the renderer reads only `properties`, so such a schema could not render regardless. Noted as a deliberate scope decision, not a defect.

Both inner-element decodes use unwrap_or/unwrap_or_else, swallowing the ArgError. Deliberate and no regression: a genuinely malformed record must still fall to the pre-existing dropped/skipped counters rather than failing the whole batch. Erroring the batch on one bad element WOULD be a regression.

validate_body's scalar check was moved BEFORE the schema short-circuits, so it now runs for operations with no request schema. Initial implementation rejected every non-object, which would have broken routes taking Json<Vec<T>>. Narrowed to scalars only (string/number/bool); arrays still pass unless the schema says object. Verified validate_body has exactly ONE production caller, so the blast radius is contained.

The response path now 400s an unusable `content` instead of storing it. The elicitation stays PENDING, so the turn remains blocked until the user retries or declines - which is correct (they have not answered) and is what the new e2e/integration tests exercise. Our own frontend cannot produce this shape (resolveElicitation is typed Record<string, unknown>).

The zero-properties rule broke three pre-existing stream-lifecycle tests whose {"type":"object"} fixture was incidental scaffolding. Real blast radius beyond ask_user's own validation: ANY caller sending a field-less schema now errors. Rule kept (it is the design), fixtures corrected. See DRIFT-1.3.

The actionable-feedback integration test asserted on the assistant text assembled from the chat stream - i.e. what the STUB chose to echo, which it truncates to 200 chars. The refusal was correct but the assertion was testing the fixture's echo policy, and would have passed on a refusal whose corrective example was cut off. Retargeted to the continuation request's all_text (the bytes the backend actually sent the model) and added an untruncated-example assertion.

A conformance battery written against the implementation cannot fail on implementation-vs-design divergence. Verified the anti-tautology guard actually runs: the battery is driven against a closure reproducing helpers.rs:302-305 verbatim (the code as it shipped) and the test REQUIRES that to panic. Confirmed green.

The bounded-unwrap test built a 50-layer nesting; each re-encode escapes the previous layer so the FIXTURE grew ~2^n and the test HUNG - a failure mode that looks exactly like the defect under test (an unbounded unwrap). A hasty reading would have 'fixed' the production loop. Reduced to 10 layers. See DRIFT-1.8.

The citations conformance extractor compared the example against format!("{:?}", JsonRpcError), whose escaped quotes can never match the raw literal, so the battery failed on a correct message. The weaker fix (relaxing the battery's example assertion) would have removed the only mechanism enforcing the actionable-message rule at all thirteen sites. Read .message instead.

TESTS.md TEST-32 claimed the two lit_search INNER-element paths were covered, but the first implementation pass decoded only the top-level array arguments - the claim exceeded the code (a phantom leg). Both loops now decode per element. See DRIFT-1.6.

Checked whether any #[derive(JsonSchema)] type changed shape and would require an OpenAPI regen. RespondToElicitationRequest.content stays Option<Value>; requested_schema stays Value on both the notification and the SSE payload; no REST handler signature changed. No regen implied; types_ts_parity unaffected.

Helper placement checked against the codebase convention: common/tokens.rs is the precedent (small, pure, domain-neutral, unit-tested, hung off common/mod.rs). utils/ holds I/O and network infra. modules/mcp/utils is a PRIVATE mod and unreachable from citations/lit_search/control_mcp.

The new no-fields card reuses the existing Card + Button kit primitives and the sibling cancelled-card structure, so it inherits their accessible names and focus handling; both actions are real <Button>s with text labels (no icon-only control, no div-onClick). Verified by npm run check (lint:guardrails + icon-action + kit-manifest all green).

The degraded-state copy states the cause and the user's options in plain language and matches the voice of the existing cancelled card. The accept action is labelled 'Accept without values' rather than a bare 'Submit', so the user is not misled into thinking they answered.
